claims.text: Homogenized Al0.7CoCrFeNi is a eutectic alloy with a dual-phase lamellar FCC/B2 microstructure.
The initial FCC/B2 lamellae have incoherent interfaces.
The initial alloy is strong but brittle because interfacial stress concentration promotes cracking.
Treatment at approximately 6 GPa and 1473 K for 2 hours in a hexahedron-anvil apparatus will topologically transform the lamellar microstructure into a hierarchical pattern.
The proposed HPHT treatment will replace incoherent FCC/B2 boundaries with coherent interfaces.
Coherent FCC/B2 interfaces will permit dislocation transfer from the soft FCC phase into the hard B2 phase.
Shockley partial dislocations will transfer across the coherent FCC/B2 interfaces.
Perfect dislocations will transfer across the coherent FCC/B2 interfaces.
Dislocation transfer across coherent interfaces will alleviate interfacial stress concentrations that would otherwise nucleate cracks.
The transformed structure will promote stacking-fault-mediated deformation.
The transformed structure will promote deformation twinning.
The coherent hierarchical structure will produce a more homogeneous strain distribution.
The HPHT-treated alloy will have significantly lower microcrack density than the baseline alloy.
The treated alloy will exhibit elongated crack-propagation paths instead of isolated microcracks.
At high strain, GND densities in the FCC and B2 phases of the treated alloy will converge.
The treated alloy will gain ductility without sacrificing strength.
Conventional thermal-mechanical treatments such as cold rolling and annealing fail to produce the same coherent hierarchical interfaces.
The specified pressure and temperature are below the stability limits for FCC/B2 phase decomposition, amorphization, or melting.
